title: Garlic: modeled ₹977/qtl left, Solan → Bhuntar
summary: January 2022: reported garlic prices at Solan and Bhuntar imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 78% of 18 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹977 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 70 same-variety market pairs screened for garlic in January 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Bhuntar report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2022
scenes.caption: Solan (Himachal Pradesh) and Bhuntar (Himachal Pradesh) both reported garlic prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 18 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Solan reported a median ₹4,200 per quintal. Bhuntar reported a median ₹5,500 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,200/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,200 per quintal, and Bhuntar was dearer on 89% of days.

scenes.headline: 298 km by road
scenes.caption: 298 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~6 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹64/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹656 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹378 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Bhuntar report, the rule selects 15 of 18 modeled shipping days. 12 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹977 per quintal (₹668 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Garlic route from Solan to Bhuntar was positive on 78% of matched days in January 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹97,700, or ₹66,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to garlic
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹64/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Garlic route from Solan to Bhuntar was positive on 78% of matched days in January 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹97,700, or ₹66,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
